4//! Primitives for creating tiles.
5
6use crate::third_party::vello_common::flatten::Line;
7use alloc::vec;
8use alloc::vec::Vec;
9use fearless_simd::*;
10#[cfg(any())]
11use peniko::kurbo::common::FloatFuncs as _;
12
13/// T-op bit
14const T: u32 = 0b00001;
15/// B-ottom bit
16const B: u32 = 0b00010;
17/// L-eft bit
18const L: u32 = 0b00100;
19/// R-ight bit
20const R: u32 = 0b01000;
21/// W-inding bit
22const W: u32 = 0b10000;
23
24/// Shift amount corresponding to the bottom bit.
25const BOT_SHIFT: u32 = B.trailing_zeros();
26/// Shift amount corresponding to the left bit.
27const LEFT_SHIFT: u32 = L.trailing_zeros();
28/// Shift amount corresponding to the right bit.
29const RIGHT_SHIFT: u32 = R.trailing_zeros();
30/// Shift amount corresponding to the winding bit.
31const WINDING_SHIFT: u32 = W.trailing_zeros();
32
33/// Mask for all intersection and winding bits (Bits 0-4).
34const INTERSECTION_MASK: u32 = W | R | L | B | T;
35/// Shift amount corresponding to the intersection bits.
36const INT_MASK_SHIFT: u32 = INTERSECTION_MASK.count_ones();
37
38/// The max number of lines per path.
39///
40/// Trying to render a path with more lines than this may result in visual artifacts.
41pub const MAX_LINES_PER_PATH: u32 = 1 << (32 - INT_MASK_SHIFT);
42
43/// A logical grouping of arrays used for culled tile processing,
44#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
45pub struct CulledWindings {
46    /// Fractional winding coverage for each individual scanline in a row.
47    pub partial: Vec<[f32; Tile::HEIGHT as usize]>,
48    // Note that this will cause issues if we have windings greater/less than i8,
49    // but this should only occur in pathological cases.
50    /// Accumulated integer winding deltas for each tile row.
51    pub coarse: Vec<i8>,
52    /// Bitmask tracking which rows contain active geometry or winding data.
53    pub active: Vec<u32>,
54    /// Flag indicating if any geometry was early-culled outside the viewport.
55    pub culled: bool,
56}
57
58impl CulledWindings {
59    /// Number of bits in a single active mask word.
60    const WORD_BITS: usize = 32;
61    /// Bit shift equivalent to dividing by `WORD_BITS` (2^5 = 32).
62    const WORD_SHIFT: usize = 5;
63    /// Bitmask equivalent to modulo `WORD_BITS` (32 - 1 = 31).
64    const WORD_MASK: usize = 31;
65
66    /// Constructor chained to `Tiles`' constructor and matches its lifetime. Since `Tiles` itself
67    /// matches the lifetime of `StripGenerator`, we know that the viewport dimensions will never
68    /// change, and thus the backing vecs never need to be resized. (For now).
69    pub fn new(height: u16) -> Self {
70        let height_usize = height as usize;
71        let tile_height = Tile::HEIGHT as usize;
72        let num_rows = height_usize.div_ceil(tile_height);
73        let num_bits = num_rows.div_ceil(Self::WORD_BITS);
74
75        Self { partial: vec![[0.0; Tile::HEIGHT as usize]; num_rows], coarse: vec![0; num_rows], active: vec![0; num_bits], culled: false }
76    }
77
78    /// Clears but does not resize
79    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
80        // TODO: Maybe consider tracking touched regions and only resetting those
81        // instead of always the full array?
82        if self.culled {
83            self.partial.fill([0.0; Tile::HEIGHT as usize]);
84            self.coarse.fill(0);
85            self.active.fill(0);
86            self.culled = false;
87        }
88    }
89
90    /// Marks if a row was culled early for faster traversal in strip generation.
91    #[inline(always)]
92    pub fn mark_row_active(&mut self, row_idx: usize) {
93        self.active[row_idx >> Self::WORD_SHIFT] |= 1 << (row_idx & Self::WORD_MASK);
94    }
95
96    /// Bulk marks a range of rows as active [`start_row`, `end_row`).
97    #[inline(always)]
98    pub fn mark_row_range_active(&mut self, start_row: usize, end_row: usize) {
99        if start_row >= end_row {
100            return;
101        }
102
103        let start_word = start_row >> Self::WORD_SHIFT;
104        let end_word = (end_row - 1) >> Self::WORD_SHIFT;
105
106        if start_word == end_word {
107            // All bits fall within the same u32 word
108            let shift = start_row & Self::WORD_MASK;
109            let count = end_row - start_row;
110            let mask = if count == Self::WORD_BITS { u32::MAX } else { ((1_u32 << count) - 1) << shift };
111            self.active[start_word] |= mask;
112        } else {
113            // Bits span multiple words: handle start, full middle words, and end
114            self.active[start_word] |= u32::MAX << (start_row & Self::WORD_MASK);
115
116            self.active[(start_word + 1)..end_word].fill(u32::MAX);
117
118            let end_shift = ((end_row - 1) & Self::WORD_MASK) + 1;
119            let mask = if end_shift == Self::WORD_BITS { u32::MAX } else { (1_u32 << end_shift) - 1 };
120            self.active[end_word] |= mask;
121        }
122    }
123
124    /// Calls `f` on active rows in the range [`start`, `end`).
125    #[inline(always)]
126    pub fn for_active_rows_in_range<F>(&self, start: usize, end: usize, mut f: F)
127    where
128        F: FnMut(usize),
129    {
130        if start >= end {
131            return;
132        }
133
134        let start_word = start >> Self::WORD_SHIFT;
135        let end_word = (end - 1) >> Self::WORD_SHIFT;
136
137        let mut process_word = |mut word: u32, word_idx: usize| {
138            while word != 0 {
139                let bit = word.trailing_zeros();
140                word &= !(1_u32 << bit);
141                f((word_idx << Self::WORD_SHIFT) + bit as usize);
142            }
143        };
144
145        let end_limit = ((end - 1) & Self::WORD_MASK) + 1;
146        let end_mask = if end_limit == Self::WORD_BITS { u32::MAX } else { (1_u32 << end_limit) - 1 };
147
148        // Start Word
149        {
150            let mut word = self.active[start_word];
151            let start_bit = start & Self::WORD_MASK;
152            word &= !((1_u32 << start_bit) - 1);
153
154            if start_word == end_word {
155                word &= end_mask;
156            }
157
158            process_word(word, start_word);
159        }
160
161        // Middle Words & End Word
162        if start_word < end_word {
163            for (word_idx, &word_val) in self.active.iter().enumerate().take(end_word).skip(start_word + 1) {
164                process_word(word_val, word_idx);
165            }
166
167            // End Word
168            process_word(self.active[end_word] & end_mask, end_word);
169        }
170    }
171}

173/// A tile represents an aligned area on the pixmap, used to subdivide the viewport into sub-areas
174/// (currently 4x4) and analyze line intersections inside each such area.
175///
176/// Keep in mind that it is possible to have multiple tiles with the same index,
177/// namely if we have multiple lines crossing the same 4x4 area!
178///
179/// # Note
180///
181/// This struct is `#[repr(C)]`, but the byte order of its fields is dependent on the endianness of
182/// the compilation target.
183#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
184#[repr(C)]
185pub struct Tile {
186    // The field ordering is important.
187    //
188    // The given ordering (variant over little and big endian compilation targets), ensures that
189    // `Tile::to_bits` doesn't do any actual work, as the ordering of the fields is such that the
190    // numeric value of a `Tile` in memory is identical as returned by that method. This allows
191    // for, e.g., comparison and sorting.
192    #[cfg(target_endian = "big")]
193    /// The index of the tile in the y direction.
194    pub y: u16,
195
196    #[cfg(target_endian = "big")]
197    /// The index of the tile in the x direction.
198    pub x: u16,
199
200    /// The index of the line this tile belongs to into the line buffer, intersection data,
201    /// and winding data packed together.
202    ///
203    /// The layout is:
204    /// - **Bits 0-4 (5 bits):** Intersection and Winding Mask (`W | R | L | B | T`).
205    ///   - Bit 0 (mask `0b00001`): Intersects top edge (T)
206    ///   - Bit 1 (mask `0b00010`): Intersects bottom edge (B)
207    ///   - Bit 2 (mask `0b00100`): Intersects left edge (L)
208    ///   - Bit 3 (mask `0b01000`): Intersects right edge (R)
209    ///   - Bit 4 (mask `0b10000`): Winding (W) - 1 if crosses top edge.
210    /// - **Bits 5-31 (27 bits):** The line index (`line_idx`).
211    ///
212    /// **Sorting Note:** The `line_idx` occupies the higher bits to ensure that when sorting
213    /// tiles with the same (x, y) coordinates, they are sorted by their line index first,
214    /// and then by their intersection mask.
215    pub packed_winding_line_idx: u32,
216
217    #[cfg(target_endian = "little")]
218    /// The index of the tile in the x direction.
219    pub x: u16,
220
221    #[cfg(target_endian = "little")]
222    /// The index of the tile in the y direction.
223    pub y: u16,
224}
225
226impl Tile {
227    /// The width of a tile in pixels.
228    pub const WIDTH: u16 = 4;
229
230    /// The height of a tile in pixels.
231    pub const HEIGHT: u16 = 4;
232
233    /// A special tile used to signal the end of a tile stream during rendering.
234    pub const SENTINEL: Self = Self::new(u16::MAX, u16::MAX, 0, 0);
235
236    /// Create a new tile.
237    /// `x` and `y` will be clamped to the largest possible coordinate if they are too large.
238    ///
239    /// `line_idx` must be smaller than [`MAX_LINES_PER_PATH`].
240    #[inline]
241    pub fn new_clamped(x: u16, y: u16, line_idx: u32, intersection_mask: u32) -> Self {
242        Self::new(
243            // Make sure that x and y stay in range when multiplying
244            // with the tile width and height during strips generation.
245            x.min(u16::MAX / Self::WIDTH),
246            y.min(u16::MAX / Self::HEIGHT),
247            line_idx,
248            intersection_mask,
249        )
250    }
251
252    /// The base tile constructor
253    ///
254    /// Unlike [`Self::new_clamped`], this constructor stores `x` and `y` exactly as provided.
255    /// Callers must ensure these coordinates do not exceed the limits required by downstream
256    /// processing (typically `u16::MAX / WIDTH` and `u16::MAX / HEIGHT`).
257    #[inline]
258    pub const fn new(x: u16, y: u16, line_idx: u32, intersection_mask: u32) -> Self {
259        #[cfg(debug_assertions)]
260        if line_idx >= MAX_LINES_PER_PATH {
261            panic!("Max. number of lines per path exceeded.");
262        }
263        // The intersection_mask is expected to contain bits 0-4 (T, B, L, R, W).
264        // We pack line_idx into the high bits (5-31) and intersection_mask into low bits (0-4).
265        Self { x, y, packed_winding_line_idx: (line_idx << INT_MASK_SHIFT) | intersection_mask }
266    }
267
268    /// Check whether two tiles are at the same location.
269    #[inline]
270    pub const fn same_loc(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
271        self.same_row(other) && self.x == other.x
272    }
273
274    /// Check whether `self` is adjacent to the left of `other`.
275    #[inline]
276    pub const fn prev_loc(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
277        self.same_row(other) && self.x + 1 == other.x
278    }
279
280    /// Check whether two tiles are on the same row.
281    #[inline]
282    pub const fn same_row(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
283        self.y == other.y
284    }
285
286    /// The index of the line this tile belongs to into the line buffer.
287    ///
288    /// Returns the high 27 bits.
289    #[inline]
290    pub const fn line_idx(&self) -> u32 {
291        self.packed_winding_line_idx >> INT_MASK_SHIFT
292    }
293
294    /// Whether the line crosses the top edge of the tile.
295    ///
296    /// Lines making this crossing increment or decrement the coarse tile winding, depending on the
297    /// line direction.
298    ///
299    /// Checks Bit 4 (Winding).
300    #[inline]
301    pub const fn winding(&self) -> bool {
302        (self.packed_winding_line_idx & W) != 0
303    }
304
305    /// The 5 bits of intersection and winding data.
306    #[inline]
307    pub const fn intersection_mask(&self) -> u32 {
308        self.packed_winding_line_idx & INTERSECTION_MASK
309    }
310
311    /// Whether the line intersects the top edge of the tile.
312    #[inline]
313    pub const fn intersects_top(&self) -> bool {
314        (self.intersection_mask() & T) != 0
315    }
316
317    /// Whether the line intersects the bottom edge of the tile.
318    #[inline]
319    pub const fn intersects_bottom(&self) -> bool {
320        (self.intersection_mask() & B) != 0
321    }
322
323    /// Whether the line intersects the left edge of the tile.
324    #[inline]
325    pub const fn intersects_left(&self) -> bool {
326        (self.intersection_mask() & L) != 0
327    }
328
329    /// Whether the line intersects the right edge of the tile.
330    #[inline]
331    pub const fn intersects_right(&self) -> bool {
332        (self.intersection_mask() & R) != 0
333    }
334
335    /// Return the `u64` representation of this tile.
336    ///
337    /// This is the u64 interpretation of `(y, x, packed_winding_line_idx)` where `y` is the
338    /// most-significant part of the number and `packed_winding_line_idx` the least significant.
339    #[inline(always)]
340    const fn to_bits(self) -> u64 {
341        // Note that for correct rendering, tiles only need to be sorted on `(y, x)`. Sorting on
342        // the line index in addition to the coordinate improves data locality in strip rendering.
343        // This is trading off increased sorting time for decreased strip rendering time. How the
344        // trade-off falls is scene-dependent.
345        //
346        // This operation compiles to a no-op: `Tile`'s field order is such that this is exactly
347        // the in-memory representation.
348        ((self.y as u64) << 48) | ((self.x as u64) << 32) | self.packed_winding_line_idx as u64
349    }
350
351    /// Whether a tile is a sentinel tile
352    //
353    // A tile produced organically by a make_tiles call can never have this coordinate because of
354    // the division by tile size on creation, so checking on x is sufficient to identify it.
355    #[inline(always)]
356    pub const fn is_sentinel(&self) -> bool {
357        self.x == u16::MAX
358    }
359}
360
361impl PartialEq for Tile {
362    #[inline(always)]
363    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
364        self.to_bits() == other.to_bits()
365    }
366}
367
368impl Ord for Tile {
369    #[inline(always)]
370    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> core::cmp::Ordering {
371        self.to_bits().cmp(&other.to_bits())
372    }
373}
374
375impl PartialOrd for Tile {
376    #[inline(always)]
377    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<core::cmp::Ordering> {
378        Some(self.cmp(other))
379    }
380}
381
382impl Eq for Tile {}

384/// Handles the tiling of paths.
385#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
386pub struct Tiles {
387    tile_buf: Vec<Tile>,
388    level: Level,
389    sorted: bool,
390    /// Auxiliary data tracking row windings and active rows for early culling.
391    pub windings: CulledWindings,
392}
393
394impl Tiles {
395    /// Create a new tiles container.
396    pub fn new(level: Level, height: u16) -> Self {
397        Self { tile_buf: vec![], level, sorted: false, windings: CulledWindings::new(height) }
398    }
399
400    /// Get the number of tiles in the container.
401    pub fn len(&self) -> u32 {
402        self.tile_buf.len() as u32
403    }
404
405    /// Returns `true` if the container has no tiles.
406    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
407        self.tile_buf.is_empty()
408    }
409
410    /// Returns `true` if any geometry was early-culled outside the viewport.
411    pub fn has_culled_tiles(&self) -> bool {
412        self.windings.culled
413    }
414
415    /// Reset the tiles' container.
416    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
417        self.windings.reset();
418        self.tile_buf.clear();
419        self.sorted = false;
420    }
421
422    /// Sort the tiles in the container.
423    pub fn sort_tiles(&mut self) {
424        self.sorted = true;
425        // To enable auto-vectorization.
426        self.level.dispatch(|_| self.tile_buf.sort_unstable());
427    }
428
429    /// Get the tile at a certain index.
430    ///
431    /// Panics if the container hasn't been sorted before.
432    #[inline]
433    pub fn get(&self, index: u32) -> &Tile {
434        assert!(self.sorted, "attempted to call `get` before sorting the tile container.");
435
436        &self.tile_buf[index as usize]
437    }
438
439    /// Iterate over the tiles in sorted order.
440    ///
441    /// Panics if the container hasn't been sorted before.
442    #[inline]
443    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Tile> {
444        assert!(self.sorted, "attempted to call `iter` before sorting the tile container.");
445
446        self.tile_buf.iter()
447    }
448
449    /// Generates tile commands for Analytic Anti-Aliasing rasterization. Unlike the MSAA path, this
450    /// function performs "coarse binning" to simply identify every tile a line segment traverses.
451    /// It encodes the line index and winding direction, delegating the precise calculation of pixel
452    /// coverage to `strip::render`.
453    pub fn make_tiles_analytic_aa(&mut self, level: Level, lines: &[Line], width: u16, height: u16) -> bool {
454        dispatch!(level, simd => self.make_tiles_analytic_aa_impl::<_>(
455            simd,
456            lines,
457            width,
458            height,
459        ))
460    }
461
462    fn make_tiles_analytic_aa_impl<S: Simd>(&mut self, s: S, lines: &[Line], width: u16, height: u16) -> bool {
463        self.reset();
464
465        if width == 0 || height == 0 {
466            return self.windings.culled;
467        }
468
469        debug_assert!(
470            lines.len() <= MAX_LINES_PER_PATH as usize,
471            "Max. number of lines per path exceeded. Max is {}, got {}.",
472            MAX_LINES_PER_PATH,
473            lines.len()
474        );
475
476        let tile_columns = width.div_ceil(Tile::WIDTH);
477        let tile_rows = height.div_ceil(Tile::HEIGHT);
478
479        let px_top = f32x4::from_slice(s, &[0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0]);
480        let px_bottom = px_top + f32x4::splat(s, 1.0);
481        let simd_zero = f32x4::splat(s, 0.0);
482        let tile_height_f32 = Tile::HEIGHT as f32;
483
484        for (line_idx, line) in lines.iter().take(MAX_LINES_PER_PATH as usize).enumerate() {
485            let line_idx = line_idx as u32;
486
487            let p0_x = line.p0.x / f32::from(Tile::WIDTH);
488            let p0_y = line.p0.y / f32::from(Tile::HEIGHT);
489            let p1_x = line.p1.x / f32::from(Tile::WIDTH);
490            let p1_y = line.p1.y / f32::from(Tile::HEIGHT);
491
492            let (line_left_x, line_right_x) = if p0_x < p1_x { (p0_x, p1_x) } else { (p1_x, p0_x) };
493
494            // Lines whose left-most endpoint exceed the right edge of the viewport are culled
495            if line_left_x > tile_columns as f32 {
496                continue;
497            }
498
499            let (line_top_y, line_top_x, line_bottom_y, line_bottom_x) =
500                if p0_y < p1_y { (p0_y, p0_x, p1_y, p1_x) } else { (p1_y, p1_x, p0_y, p0_x) };
501
502            // The `as u16` casts here intentionally clamp negative coordinates to 0.
503            let y_top_tiles = (line_top_y as u16).min(tile_rows);
504            let line_bottom_y_ceil = line_bottom_y.ceil();
505            let y_bottom_tiles = (line_bottom_y_ceil as u16).min(tile_rows);
506
507            // If y_top_tiles == y_bottom_tiles, then the line is either completely above or below
508            // the viewport OR it is perfectly horizontal and aligned to the tile grid, contributing
509            // no winding. In either case, it should be culled.
510            if y_top_tiles >= y_bottom_tiles {
511                // Technically, the `>` part of the `>=` is unnecessary due to clamping, but this
512                // gives stronger signal
513                continue;
514            }
515
516            let dir = if p0_y >= p1_y { 1 } else { -1 };
517            let f_dir = dir as f32;
518            let f_dir_v = f32x4::splat(s, f_dir);
519
520            macro_rules! calc_fractional_coverage {
521                ($y_idx:expr, $segment_top_y:expr, $segment_bottom_y:expr) => {{
522                    let y_idx_f32 = f32::from($y_idx);
523                    let local_y_start = ($segment_top_y - y_idx_f32) * tile_height_f32;
524                    let local_y_end = ($segment_bottom_y - y_idx_f32) * tile_height_f32;
525
526                    let start_v = f32x4::splat(s, local_y_start);
527                    let end_v = f32x4::splat(s, local_y_end);
528
529                    (px_bottom.min(end_v) - px_top.max(start_v)).max(simd_zero)
530                }};
531            }
532
533            // Lines fully to the left of the viewport are not visible but still produce winding
534            // which we record here and forward to the rendering stage.
535            if line_right_x < 0.0 {
536                let is_start_culled = line_top_y < 0.0;
537
538                // This branch is for handling the "start" of the line. In case
539                // the line reaches above the viewport, we are already in the
540                // middle so we can skip that part.
541                if !is_start_culled {
542                    self.windings.mark_row_active(y_top_tiles as usize);
543
544                    // Note: In theory, == should be enough, but just as
545                    // additional safety against numerical precision errors we
546                    // use <=.
547                    let at_top_of_tile = line_top_y <= f32::from(y_top_tiles);
548                    if at_top_of_tile {
549                        self.windings.coarse[y_top_tiles as usize] += dir;
550                    }
551
552                    let fractional_coverage = calc_fractional_coverage!(y_top_tiles, line_top_y, line_bottom_y);
553                    let target_row = &mut self.windings.partial[y_top_tiles as usize];
554                    let current = f32x4::from_slice(s, target_row);
555
556                    // See comment below on the double counting risk!
557                    let double_count = if at_top_of_tile { f_dir_v } else { f32x4::splat(s, 0.0) };
558                    let next = fractional_coverage.mul_add(f_dir_v, current - double_count);
559                    next.store_slice(target_row);
560                }
561
562                let y_start_middle = if is_start_culled { y_top_tiles } else { y_top_tiles + 1 };
563                let line_bottom_floor = line_bottom_y.floor();
564                let y_end_middle = (line_bottom_floor as u16).min(tile_rows);
565
566                for y_idx in y_start_middle..y_end_middle {
567                    self.windings.coarse[y_idx as usize] += dir;
568                }
569                self.windings.mark_row_range_active(y_start_middle as usize, y_end_middle as usize);
570
571                if line_bottom_y != line_bottom_floor
572                    && y_end_middle < tile_rows
573                    // Prevent double-processing, unless the start was off-screen and hasn't been
574                    // handled yet.
575                    && (is_start_culled || y_end_middle != y_top_tiles)
576                {
577                    self.windings.mark_row_active(y_end_middle as usize);
578                    // Ends implicitly cross the top.
579                    self.windings.coarse[y_end_middle as usize] += dir;
580                    let fractional_coverage = calc_fractional_coverage!(y_end_middle, line_top_y, line_bottom_y);
581                    let target_row = &mut self.windings.partial[y_end_middle as usize];
582                    let current = f32x4::from_slice(s, target_row);
583                    // Subtract the inverse direction to avoid double counting with the coarse winding.
584                    let next = fractional_coverage.mul_add(f_dir_v, current - f_dir_v);
585                    next.store_slice(target_row);
586                }
587
588                self.windings.culled = true;
589                continue;
590            }
591
592            // Get tile coordinates for start/end points, use i32 to preserve negative coordinates.
593            let p0_tile_x = line_top_x.floor() as i32;
594            let p0_tile_y = line_top_y.floor() as i32;
595            let p1_tile_x = line_bottom_x.floor() as i32;
596            let p1_tile_y = line_bottom_y.floor() as i32;
597
598            // Special-case out lines which are fully contained within a tile.
599            let not_same_tile = p0_tile_y != p1_tile_y || p0_tile_x != p1_tile_x;
600            if not_same_tile {
601                // Case vertical lines: By definition, these cannot be horizontally crossing, and
602                // thus require no additional left-edge culling handling.
603                if line_left_x == line_right_x {
604                    let x = (line_left_x as u16).min(tile_columns.saturating_sub(1));
605
606                    // Row Start, not culled.
607                    let is_start_culled = line_top_y < 0.0;
608                    if !is_start_culled {
609                        let winding = ((f32::from(y_top_tiles) >= line_top_y) as u32) << WINDING_SHIFT;
610                        let tile = Tile::new_clamped(x, y_top_tiles, line_idx, winding);
611                        self.tile_buf.push(tile);
612                    }
613
614                    // Middle
615                    // If the start was culled, the first tile inside the viewport is a middle.
616                    let y_start = if is_start_culled { y_top_tiles } else { y_top_tiles + 1 };
617
618                    for y_idx in y_start..y_bottom_tiles {
619                        let tile = Tile::new_clamped(x, y_idx, line_idx, W);
620                        self.tile_buf.push(tile);
621                    }
622                } else {
623                    // General case, any line which crosses more than one tile and is not vertical.
624                    let dx = p1_x - p0_x;
625                    let dy = p1_y - p0_y;
626                    let x_slope = dx / dy;
627                    let dx_dir = (line_bottom_x >= line_top_x) as u32;
628                    let not_dx_dir = dx_dir ^ 1;
629
630                    let w_start_base = dx_dir << WINDING_SHIFT;
631                    let w_end_base = not_dx_dir << WINDING_SHIFT;
632
633                    let mut push_row = {
634                        #[inline(always)]
635                        |y_idx: u16, row_top_y: f32, row_bottom_y: f32, w_start: u32, w_end: u32, w_single: u32| {
636                            let row_top_x = p0_x + (row_top_y - p0_y) * x_slope;
637                            let row_bottom_x = p0_x + (row_bottom_y - p0_y) * x_slope;
638
639                            let row_left_x = f32::min(row_top_x, row_bottom_x).max(line_left_x);
640                            let row_right_x = f32::max(row_top_x, row_bottom_x).min(line_right_x);
641
642                            if row_left_x < 0.0 {
643                                self.windings.culled = true;
644
645                                if row_right_x < 0.0 {
646                                    // Although the line may cross the left edge, the rightmost point in
647                                    // this row may still be fully left of the viewport. In this case,
648                                    // record the winding and emit no tiles.
649                                    self.windings.mark_row_active(y_idx as usize);
650
651                                    let crosses_top = (w_single & W) != 0;
652                                    if crosses_top {
653                                        self.windings.coarse[y_idx as usize] += dir;
654                                    }
655
656                                    let fractional_coverage = calc_fractional_coverage!(y_idx, row_top_y, row_bottom_y);
657                                    let target_row = &mut self.windings.partial[y_idx as usize];
658                                    let current = f32x4::from_slice(s, target_row);
659
660                                    let double_count = if crosses_top { f_dir_v } else { f32x4::splat(s, 0.0) };
661                                    let next = fractional_coverage.mul_add(f_dir_v, current - double_count);
662                                    next.store_slice(target_row);
663
664                                    return;
665                                } else {
666                                    // The line crosses into the viewport in this row. Record only the
667                                    // fractional portion of the winding, as the coarse winding will
668                                    // naturally get included by the clamped tile logic!
669                                    let y_slope = dy / dx;
670                                    let y_intersect = row_top_y - (row_top_x * y_slope);
671
672                                    let (off_screen_top_y, off_screen_bottom_y) = if row_top_x < 0.0 {
673                                        (row_top_y, f32::min(row_bottom_y, y_intersect))
674                                    } else {
675                                        (f32::max(row_top_y, y_intersect), row_bottom_y)
676                                    };
677
678                                    if off_screen_top_y < off_screen_bottom_y {
679                                        self.windings.mark_row_active(y_idx as usize);
680                                        let fractional_coverage = calc_fractional_coverage!(y_idx, off_screen_top_y, off_screen_bottom_y);
681                                        let target_row = &mut self.windings.partial[y_idx as usize];
682                                        let current = f32x4::from_slice(s, target_row);
683                                        let next = fractional_coverage.mul_add(f_dir_v, current);
684                                        next.store_slice(target_row);
685                                    }
686                                }
687                            }
688
689                            let x_start = row_left_x as u16;
690                            let x_end = (row_right_x as u16).min(tile_columns.saturating_sub(1));
691
692                            if x_start <= x_end {
693                                let winding = if x_start == x_end { w_single } else { w_start };
694
695                                self.tile_buf.push(Tile::new(x_start, y_idx, line_idx, winding));
696
697                                for x_idx in x_start.saturating_add(1)..x_end {
698                                    self.tile_buf.push(Tile::new(x_idx, y_idx, line_idx, 0));
699                                }
700
701                                if x_start < x_end {
702                                    self.tile_buf.push(Tile::new(x_end, y_idx, line_idx, w_end));
703                                }
704                            }
705                        }
706                    };
707
708                    let is_start_culled = line_top_y < 0.0;
709                    if !is_start_culled {
710                        let y = f32::from(y_top_tiles);
711                        let row_bottom_y = (y + 1.0).min(line_bottom_y);
712                        let mask = ((y >= line_top_y) as u32) << WINDING_SHIFT;
713                        push_row(y_top_tiles, line_top_y, row_bottom_y, w_start_base & mask, w_end_base & mask, W & mask);
714                    }
715
716                    let y_start = if is_start_culled { y_top_tiles } else { y_top_tiles + 1 };
717
718                    for y_idx in y_start..y_bottom_tiles {
719                        let y = f32::from(y_idx);
720                        let row_bottom_y = (y + 1.0).min(line_bottom_y);
721                        push_row(y_idx, y, row_bottom_y, w_start_base, w_end_base, W);
722                    }
723                }
724            } else {
725                // Case line is fully contained within a single tile: These also cannot cross edges!
726                let tile = Tile::new_clamped(
727                    (line_left_x as u16).min(tile_columns + 1),
728                    y_top_tiles,
729                    line_idx,
730                    ((f32::from(y_top_tiles) >= line_top_y) as u32) << WINDING_SHIFT,
731                );
732                self.tile_buf.push(tile);
733            }
734        }
735
736        self.windings.culled
737    }
738
739    /// Generates tile commands for MSAA (Multisample Anti-Aliasing) rasterization.
740    ///
741    /// [ Architecture & Watertightness ]
742    /// The primary goal of this function is to establish a source of "ground truth" for line-tile
743    /// intersections. Because the downstream rasterization (MSAA) occurs in parallel, it is
744    /// critical that intersections are "watertight." If Thread A handles Tile (0,0) and Thread B
745    /// handles Tile (1,0), they must agree exactly on whether a line crosses the shared edge.
746    ///
747    /// While calculating exact intersection coordinates here is feasible, it is computationally
748    /// expensive. Instead, we defer the heavy math to the GPU/rasterizer and produce a lightweight
749    /// Intersection Bitmask. This mask unambiguously defines which edges of a tile a line segment
750    /// touches or crosses.
751    ///
752    /// [ The Intersection Bitmask (5 bits) ]
753    /// The bitmask encodes winding information and edge intersections. A line is said to
754    /// "intersect" an edge if it touches that edge AND continues into the neighboring tile.
755    ///
756    /// Bit representation:
757    /// Bit: 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 0
758    /// Val: W | R | L | B | T
759    ///
760    /// - W (Winding): Tracks whether the line touched the top edge of the tile.
761    /// - R/L/B/T: Right, Left, Bottom, and Top edge intersections.
762    pub fn make_tiles_msaa(&mut self, lines: &[Line], width: u16, height: u16) {
763        self.reset();
764
765        if width == 0 || height == 0 {
766            return;
767        }
768
769        debug_assert!(
770            lines.len() <= MAX_LINES_PER_PATH as usize,
771            "Max. number of lines per path exceeded. Max is {}, got {}.",
772            MAX_LINES_PER_PATH,
773            lines.len()
774        );
775
776        let tile_columns = width.div_ceil(Tile::WIDTH);
777        let tile_rows = height.div_ceil(Tile::HEIGHT);
778
779        for (line_idx, line) in lines.iter().take(MAX_LINES_PER_PATH as usize).enumerate() {
780            let line_idx = line_idx as u32;
781
782            let p0_x = line.p0.x / f32::from(Tile::WIDTH);
783            let p0_y = line.p0.y / f32::from(Tile::HEIGHT);
784            let p1_x = line.p1.x / f32::from(Tile::WIDTH);
785            let p1_y = line.p1.y / f32::from(Tile::HEIGHT);
786
787            let (line_left_x, line_right_x) = if p0_x < p1_x { (p0_x, p1_x) } else { (p1_x, p0_x) };
788
789            // Lines whose left-most endpoint exceed the right edge of the viewport are culled
790            if line_left_x > tile_columns as f32 {
791                continue;
792            }
793
794            let (line_top_y, line_top_x, line_bottom_y, line_bottom_x) =
795                if p0_y < p1_y { (p0_y, p0_x, p1_y, p1_x) } else { (p1_y, p1_x, p0_y, p0_x) };
796
797            // The `as u16` casts here intentionally clamp negative coordinates to 0.
798            let y_top_tiles = (line_top_y as u16).min(tile_rows);
799            let line_bottom_y_ceil = line_bottom_y.ceil();
800            let y_bottom_tiles = (line_bottom_y_ceil as u16).min(tile_rows);
801
802            // If y_top_tiles == y_bottom_tiles, then the line is either completely above or below
803            // the viewport OR it is perfectly horizontal and aligned to the tile grid, contributing
804            // no winding. In either case, it should be culled.
805            if y_top_tiles >= y_bottom_tiles {
806                continue;
807            }
808
809            // Get tile coordinates for start/end points, use i32 to preserve negative coordinates
810            let p0_tile_x = line_top_x.floor() as i32;
811            let p0_tile_y = line_top_y.floor() as i32;
812            let p1_tile_x = line_bottom_x.floor() as i32;
813
814            let p1_tile_y = if line_bottom_y == line_bottom_y_ceil { line_bottom_y as i32 - 1 } else { line_bottom_y.floor() as i32 };
815
816            // Special-case out lines which are fully contained within a tile.
817            let not_same_tile = p0_tile_y != p1_tile_y || p0_tile_x != p1_tile_x;
818            if not_same_tile {
819                // For ease of logic, special-case purely vertical tiles.
820                if line_left_x == line_right_x {
821                    let x = (line_left_x as u16).min(tile_columns.saturating_sub(1));
822
823                    // Row Start, not culled.
824                    let is_start_culled = line_top_y < 0.0;
825                    if !is_start_culled {
826                        let winding = ((f32::from(y_top_tiles) >= line_top_y) as u32) << WINDING_SHIFT;
827                        let intersection_mask = B | winding;
828                        let tile = Tile::new_clamped(x, y_top_tiles, line_idx, intersection_mask);
829                        self.tile_buf.push(tile);
830                    }
831
832                    // Middle
833                    // If the start was culled, the first tile inside the viewport is a middle.
834                    let y_start = if is_start_culled { y_top_tiles } else { y_top_tiles + 1 };
835                    let line_bottom_floor = line_bottom_y.floor();
836                    let y_end_idx = (line_bottom_floor as u16).min(tile_rows);
837
838                    if y_start < y_end_idx {
839                        let y_last = y_end_idx - 1;
840                        for y_idx in y_start..y_last {
841                            let intersection_mask = W | B | T;
842                            let tile = Tile::new_clamped(x, y_idx, line_idx, intersection_mask);
843                            self.tile_buf.push(tile);
844                        }
845
846                        // Perfect touching B case.
847                        {
848                            let is_end_tile = ((y_last as i32) == p1_tile_y) as u32;
849                            let intersection_mask = W | T | ((1 ^ is_end_tile) << BOT_SHIFT);
850                            let tile = Tile::new_clamped(x, y_last, line_idx, intersection_mask);
851                            self.tile_buf.push(tile);
852                        }
853                    }
854
855                    // Row End, handle the final tile (y_end_idx), but *only* if the line does
856                    // not perfectly end on the top edge of the tile. In the case that it does,
857                    // it gets handled by the middle logic above.
858                    if line_bottom_y != line_bottom_floor && y_end_idx < tile_rows {
859                        let intersection_mask = W | T;
860                        let tile = Tile::new_clamped(x, y_end_idx, line_idx, intersection_mask);
861                        self.tile_buf.push(tile);
862                    }
863                } else {
864                    let dx = p1_x - p0_x;
865                    let dy = p1_y - p0_y;
866                    let x_slope = dx / dy;
867                    let dx_dir = (line_bottom_x >= line_top_x) as u32;
868                    let not_dx_dir = dx_dir ^ 1;
869
870                    let w_start_base = dx_dir << WINDING_SHIFT;
871                    let w_end_base = not_dx_dir << WINDING_SHIFT;
872
873                    // Check if the line is fully within the horizontal viewport bounds. If it is,
874                    // we can skip the min/max clamping per row.
875                    let min_x = p0_x.min(p1_x);
876                    let max_x = p0_x.max(p1_x);
877                    // Note: We use >= on the right edge to ensure strictly safe integer truncation
878                    let needs_clamping = min_x < line_left_x || max_x >= line_right_x;
879
880                    // Handles the bitmask logic for start/end tiles. Invariant to clamping.
881                    macro_rules! push_edge {
882                        ($x:expr, $y:expr, $row_top_x:expr, $row_bottom_x:expr,
883                         $canonical_start:expr, $canonical_end:expr, $winding_input:expr,
884                         $check_s:tt, $check_e:expr) => {{
885                            let x_idx = $x;
886
887                            let unc_row_start = (x_idx as i32 == $canonical_start) as u32;
888                            let unc_row_end = (x_idx == $canonical_end) as u32;
889
890                            let canonical_row_start = (dx_dir & unc_row_start) | (not_dx_dir & unc_row_end);
891                            let canonical_row_end = (not_dx_dir & unc_row_start) | (dx_dir & unc_row_end);
892
893                            let start_tile = if $check_s { ((x_idx as i32 == p0_tile_x) && ($y as i32 == p0_tile_y)) as u32 } else { 0 };
894
895                            let end_tile = if $check_e { ((x_idx as i32 == p1_tile_x) && ($y as i32 == p1_tile_y)) as u32 } else { 0 };
896
897                            let mut mask = $winding_input;
898
899                            // Entrant/Exit
900                            mask |= canonical_row_start & (1 ^ start_tile);
901                            mask |= (1 ^ canonical_row_start) << not_dx_dir << LEFT_SHIFT;
902                            mask |= (canonical_row_end & (1 ^ end_tile)) << BOT_SHIFT;
903                            mask |= (1 ^ canonical_row_end) << dx_dir << LEFT_SHIFT;
904
905                            // Corner
906                            let x_left_f = x_idx as f32;
907                            let x_right_f = (x_idx + 1) as f32;
908                            let trc = (($row_top_x == x_right_f) as u32) & (1 ^ start_tile);
909                            let tlc = (($row_top_x == x_left_f) as u32) & (1 ^ start_tile);
910                            let brc = (($row_bottom_x == x_right_f) as u32) & (1 ^ end_tile);
911                            let blc = (($row_bottom_x == x_left_f) as u32) & (1 ^ end_tile);
912                            // Top left is handled specially
913                            let tie_break = tlc & (canonical_row_start ^ 1);
914
915                            mask |= (tie_break | blc) << LEFT_SHIFT;
916                            mask |= (trc | brc) << RIGHT_SHIFT;
917                            mask &= !(tie_break | trc);
918                            mask &= !((blc | brc) << BOT_SHIFT);
919
920                            self.tile_buf.push(Tile::new(x_idx, $y, line_idx, mask));
921                        }};
922                    }
923
924                    // Handles row geometry and clamping logic.
925                    macro_rules! process_row {
926                        ($y_idx:expr, $row_top_y:expr, $row_bottom_y:expr, $w_mask:expr,
927                     $check_s:tt, $check_e:tt, $clamped:tt) => {{
928                            let row_top_x = p0_x + ($row_top_y - p0_y) * x_slope;
929                            let row_bottom_x = p0_x + ($row_bottom_y - p0_y) * x_slope;
930
931                            let (row_left_x, row_right_x, x_end) = if $clamped {
932                                let lx = f32::min(row_top_x, row_bottom_x).max(line_left_x);
933                                let rx = f32::max(row_top_x, row_bottom_x).min(line_right_x);
934                                let xe = (rx as u16).min(tile_columns.saturating_sub(1));
935                                (lx, rx, xe)
936                            } else {
937                                let lx = f32::min(row_top_x, row_bottom_x);
938                                let rx = f32::max(row_top_x, row_bottom_x);
939                                let xe = rx as u16; // Safe because we checked bounds earlier
940                                (lx, rx, xe)
941                            };
942
943                            let canonical_x_start = row_left_x.floor() as i32;
944                            let canonical_x_end = row_right_x as u16;
945                            let x_start = row_left_x as u16;
946
947                            if x_start <= x_end {
948                                let is_single = (x_start == x_end) as u32;
949                                let w_left = (w_start_base | (is_single << 4)) & $w_mask;
950
951                                push_edge!(x_start, $y_idx, row_top_x, row_bottom_x, canonical_x_start, canonical_x_end, w_left, $check_s, $check_e);
952
953                                for x_idx in x_start.saturating_add(1)..x_end {
954                                    self.tile_buf.push(Tile::new(x_idx, $y_idx, line_idx, R | L));
955                                }
956
957                                if x_start < x_end {
958                                    let w_right = w_end_base & $w_mask;
959                                    push_edge!(
960                                        x_end,
961                                        $y_idx,
962                                        row_top_x,
963                                        row_bottom_x,
964                                        canonical_x_start,
965                                        canonical_x_end,
966                                        w_right,
967                                        $check_s,
968                                        $check_e
969                                    );
970                                }
971                            }
972                        }};
973                    }
974
975                    // Central macro
976                    macro_rules! run_loops {
977                        ($clamped:tt) => {{
978                            // Top Row
979                            let is_start_culled = line_top_y < 0.0;
980                            if !is_start_culled {
981                                let y = f32::from(y_top_tiles);
982                                let row_bottom_y = (y + 1.0).min(line_bottom_y);
983                                let mask = ((y >= line_top_y) as u32) << WINDING_SHIFT;
984                                process_row!(y_top_tiles, line_top_y, row_bottom_y, mask, true, true, $clamped);
985                            }
986
987                            let y_start_middle = if is_start_culled { y_top_tiles } else { y_top_tiles + 1 };
988                            let line_bottom_floor = line_bottom_y.floor();
989                            let y_end_middle = (line_bottom_floor as u16).min(tile_rows);
990                            let has_separate_bottom_row =
991                                line_bottom_y != line_bottom_floor && y_end_middle < tile_rows && (is_start_culled || y_end_middle != y_top_tiles);
992
993                            if y_start_middle < y_end_middle {
994                                for y_idx in y_start_middle..y_end_middle {
995                                    let y = f32::from(y_idx);
996                                    let row_bottom_y = (y + 1.0).min(line_bottom_y);
997                                    let is_last_middle = y_idx == y_end_middle - 1;
998                                    let check_end = is_last_middle && !has_separate_bottom_row;
999
1000                                    process_row!(y_idx, y, row_bottom_y, u32::MAX, false, check_end, $clamped);
1001                                }
1002                            }
1003
1004                            // Bottom Row
1005                            if has_separate_bottom_row {
1006                                let y_idx = y_end_middle;
1007                                let y = f32::from(y_idx);
1008                                process_row!(y_idx, y, line_bottom_y, u32::MAX, false, true, $clamped);
1009                            }
1010                        }};
1011                    }
1012
1013                    if needs_clamping {
1014                        run_loops!(true);
1015                    } else {
1016                        run_loops!(false);
1017                    }
1018                }
1019            } else {
1020                // Case: Line is fully contained within a single tile.
1021                let tile = Tile::new_clamped(
1022                    (line_left_x as u16).min(tile_columns + 1),
1023                    y_top_tiles,
1024                    line_idx,
1025                    ((f32::from(y_top_tiles) >= line_top_y) as u32) << WINDING_SHIFT,
1026                );
1027                self.tile_buf.push(tile);
1028            }
1029        }
1030    }
1031}

1033#[cfg(any())]
1034mod tests {
1035    use crate::third_party::vello_common::flatten::{FlattenCtx, Line, Point, fill};
1036    use crate::third_party::vello_common::geometry::RectU16;
1037    use crate::third_party::vello_common::kurbo::{Affine, BezPath};
1038    use crate::third_party::vello_common::tile::CulledWindings;
1039    use crate::third_party::vello_common::tile::{B, L, R, T, Tile, Tiles, W};
1040    use fearless_simd::Level;
1041    use std::vec::Vec;
1042
1043    const VIEW_DIM: u16 = 100;
1044    const F_V_DIM: f32 = VIEW_DIM as f32;
1045
1046    impl Tiles {
1047        fn assert_tiles_match(&mut self, lines: &[Line], width: u16, height: u16, expected: &[Tile]) {
1048            self.make_tiles_msaa(lines, width, height);
1049            assert_eq!(self.tile_buf, expected, "MSAA: Tile buffer mismatch");
1050
1051            self.make_tiles_analytic_aa(Level::baseline(), lines, width, height);
1052            check_analytic_aa_matches(&self.tile_buf, expected);
1053        }
1054    }
1055
1056    fn check_analytic_aa_matches(actual: &[Tile], expected: &[Tile]) {
1057        assert_eq!(actual.len(), expected.len(), "Analytic AA: Tile count mismatch.");
1058
1059        for (i, (got, want)) in actual.iter().zip(expected.iter()).enumerate() {
1060            assert_eq!(got.x, want.x, "Analytic AA: Tile[{}] X mismatch", i);
1061            assert_eq!(got.y, want.y, "Analytic AA: Tile[{}] Y mismatch", i);
1062            assert_eq!(got.line_idx(), want.line_idx(), "Analytic AA: Tile[{}] Line Index mismatch", i);
1063
1064            let got_winding = got.packed_winding_line_idx & W;
1065            let want_winding = want.packed_winding_line_idx & W;
1066            assert_eq!(got_winding, want_winding, "Analytic AA: Tile[{}] Winding mismatch", i);
1067        }
1068    }

1647    #[cfg(any())]
1648    fn test_culled_windings_new_and_reset() {
1649        let mut windings = CulledWindings::new(100);
1650        assert_eq!(windings.partial.len(), 25);
1651        assert_eq!(windings.coarse.len(), 25);
1652        assert_eq!(windings.active.len(), 1);
1653
1654        windings.coarse[0] = 1;
1655        windings.active[0] = 0xFF;
1656        windings.culled = true;
1657
1658        windings.reset();
1659        assert_eq!(windings.coarse[0], 0);
1660        assert_eq!(windings.active[0], 0);
1661
1662        windings.coarse[0] = 1;
1663        windings.active[0] = 0xFF;
1664        windings.culled = false;
1665
1666        windings.reset();
1667        assert_eq!(windings.coarse[0], 1);
1668        assert_eq!(windings.active[0], 0xFF);
1669    }
1670
1671    #[cfg(any())]
1672    fn test_mark_row_active() {
1673        let mut windings = CulledWindings::new(200);
1674        windings.mark_row_active(0);
1675        windings.mark_row_active(5);
1676        windings.mark_row_active(31);
1677        windings.mark_row_active(32);
1678        assert_eq!(windings.active[0], (1 << 0) | (1 << 5) | (1 << 31));
1679        assert_eq!(windings.active[1], 1 << 0);
1680    }

1749    #[cfg(any())]
1750    fn sort_test() {
1751        let mut lines: Vec<Line> = Vec::new();
1752        let mut tiles = Tiles::new(Level::baseline(), VIEW_DIM);
1753
1754        let step = 4.0;
1755        let mut y = F_V_DIM - 10.0;
1756        while y > 10.0 {
1757            lines.push(Line { p0: Point { x: F_V_DIM - 10.0, y }, p1: Point { x: 10.0, y } });
1758
1759            lines.push(Line { p0: Point { x: F_V_DIM - 12.0, y }, p1: Point { x: 12.0, y } });
1760
1761            y -= step;
1762        }
1763
1764        tiles.make_tiles_msaa(&lines, VIEW_DIM, VIEW_DIM);
1765        assert!(tiles.tile_buf.first().unwrap().y > tiles.tile_buf.last().unwrap().y);
1766        tiles.sort_tiles();
1767        check_sorted(&tiles.tile_buf);
1768
1769        tiles.make_tiles_analytic_aa(Level::baseline(), &lines, VIEW_DIM, VIEW_DIM);
1770        assert!(tiles.tile_buf.first().unwrap().y > tiles.tile_buf.last().unwrap().y);
1771        tiles.sort_tiles();
1772        check_sorted(&tiles.tile_buf);
1773    }
1774
1775    fn check_sorted(buf: &[Tile]) {
1776        for i in 0..buf.len() - 1 {
1777            let current = buf[i];
1778            let next = buf[i + 1];
1779
1780            if current.y > next.y {
1781                panic!("Sort Failure [Y]: Tile[{}] (y={}) > Tile[{}] (y={})", i, current.y, i + 1, next.y);
1782            }
1783
1784            if current.y == next.y {
1785                if current.x > next.x {
1786                    panic!("Sort Failure [X]: at Row y={}, Tile[{}] (x={}) > Tile[{}] (x={})", current.y, i, current.x, i + 1, next.x);
1787                }
1788
1789                if current.x == next.x && current.packed_winding_line_idx > next.packed_winding_line_idx {
1790                    panic!(
1791                        "Sort Failure [Payload]: at {}x{}, Tile[{}] (val={}) > Tile[{}] (val={})",
1792                        current.x,
1793                        current.y,
1794                        i,
1795                        current.packed_winding_line_idx,
1796                        i + 1,
1797                        next.packed_winding_line_idx
1798                    );
1799                }
1800            }
1801        }
1802    }
1803}
